Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

mlvtoolbox 0.3.0

Documentation

  • vignette("getting-started") is the one installed vignette. The guides to junctions, the medial axis, MLV compatibility, workflows, line extraction and stimulus design are articles on the package website (https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/articles/), which keeps the installed documentation small (about 1.2 MB, down from 12.6 MB).

Qualified against stored MATLAB outputs

  • The package was compared with outputs the original lab computed in MATLAB for 3,017 line drawings (2,757 with medial-axis scores). Published-compatible options now reproduce them: detect_junctions(rule = "mlv2023") matches 395,125 of 395,134 junctions exactly, and compute_mat(aof = "mlv2023", morphology = "hmt8", branch_rule = "mlv2023", threshold_angle = asin(0.3 * pi / 2) * 180 / pi) reproduces Forest_DBW’s distance map, flux and skeleton exactly and 99.1-99.4% of all stored per-pixel symmetry scores within 1e-4; with estimator = "mlv2023" all 2,284,239 stored segment orientations, lengths and curvatures agree within 1e-9. See docs/PARITY.md.

Line drawings from images

  • New extract_lines() turns a photograph or an image of a painting into a binary ink mask: CIE L* lightness, an anisotropic Kuwahara pre-filter against brush texture, the structure-tensor edge tangent flow, a flow-based difference of Gaussians integrated along the flow, and the XDoG threshold (Kyprianidis, Kang and Döllner 2009; Kyprianidis and Döllner 2008; Kang, Lee and Chui 2007; Winnemöller, Kyprianidis and Olsen 2012). Two further steps are this package’s own: lines are placed on edges rather than in the dark-side XDoG band, and thin dark or light strokes are drawn once, as their centre lines. The default pre-filter removes dark strokes thinner than about 2 pixels that do not lie along a pixel row or column, so use smooth = 0 for thin line art. It is deterministic and needs no model weights or new dependencies. Without the pre-filter, quarter turns and reflections of the image transform every stage exactly; with it, the intermediate images agree to rounding and the masks have agreed exactly in every test. The mask records its definition, "fdog-xdog-1", and every parameter in an "extraction" attribute.
  • xdog_lines() is the same extractor shaped as a trace_rgb() backend, and line_extraction_stages() returns the intermediate images.
  • A positive junction_gap enables an optional repair for short gaps at occlusion junctions (#2). A bridge needs supporting edge contrast in the original image. The repaired mode records "fdog-xdog-repair-1" and its gap limit. A zero gap keeps the existing "fdog-xdog-1" definition.
  • trace_rgb() records a backend’s "extraction" attribute, when present, as source$provider_version and source$extraction_parameters.
  • feature_spec(extraction = list(lines = list(...))) fixes the line extractor’s parameters; the specification records definitions["lines"], trace_rgb() passes the parameters to the backend and checks its output, and specifications naming another version of the extractor are rejected. With any specification, trace_rgb() refuses a backend whose "extraction" attribute names a version other than the specification’s provider_version. Specifications without line settings are unchanged.
  • New vignette line-extraction (“From an image to a line drawing”), with a public-domain (CC0) painting from The Cleveland Museum of Art bundled in inst/extdata.

Behaviour changes (new default methods)

The defaults now follow the alternative definitions recorded as MLV-M018-M032 in DIFFERENCES.md (for example, junctions and branch scores that do not depend on contour direction, and curvature that counts each vertex turn once); the mlv2023 options keep the published behaviour. Feature specifications record the new method definitions, so specifications and cached MATs from 0.2.x are rejected and must be rebuilt.

  • Curvature: the default estimator is now vertex turning (estimator = "turning") in feature_spec() and in every specification-free call (as.data.frame(), compute_contour_properties(), contour_statistics(), feature_table(), predict_contours(), average_property(), plotting and feature_density()). Each vertex turn is spread once over its dual cell, the half-segments on either side of the vertex. Segment tables keep one row per input segment for every estimator; with "turning" and "arclength" a segment’s curvature is its mean curvature (the exact integral of the density over the segment divided by its length), with a signed mean in signed_curvature; curvature_profile() returns the piecewise density, and histograms integrate it exactly. The published estimator, now estimator = "mlv2023", gives each segment the whole turn to the next segment divided by its own length and repeats the previous turn on a contour’s last segment: the last vertex of every contour is counted twice (a 90 degree apex integrates to 180 degrees), the closing vertex of a closed contour is not counted, and values depend on sampling (MLV-M032). Turning has no tuning parameter and gives sampling-stable histograms: a circle of radius 10 drawn with 16, 32, 64 or 128 vertices, regularly or with alternating 1 : 2 spacing, puts all its length in one curvature bin (4.43-8.54 deg/px of 8), whereas mlv2023 splits the alternating circles between 2.09-4.43 and 8.54-15.76. "arclength" remains for curvature at a stated spatial scale. Specifications state their estimator, so a specification built when mlv2023 was the default keeps computing mlv2023 values; specification-free feature schemas now record the curvature definition in effect (vertex-dual-1 or mlv2023-port-0.1.1), so models bound to 0.2.x specification-free tables are rejected unless estimator = "mlv2023" is given. compute_contour_properties(estimator = ) records its choice on the drawing (curvature_estimator), and later calls on that drawing that give neither spec nor estimator use it; geometry operations keep the choice and drop derived measurements. The turning estimator accepts exact retracing (an unsigned 180 degree turn, signed value NA), which occurs in 178 of the 3,017 stored MLV drawings; contour_turning() and the arc-length estimator still reject it. Specification-free turning histograms are computed in the fused native pass (12,000 segments: 2.1 ms vs 1.9 ms for "mlv2023").

  • Histograms: a value within 1e-9 × max(1, |edge|) of a bin edge, in the coordinate in which the bins are equally spaced (degrees, log10(1 + x) or the raw value), is binned as if exactly on the edge, so the upper-bin rule applies and mathematically equal values share a bin on every platform (for example a computed junction gap of 59.999999999999943 and an exact 60 degrees). R and the fused native kernel apply the same rule with the same arithmetic. Rounding residue is about 1e-13 relative or less; the tolerance is far below any real measurement difference. Snapping is a numerical robustness fix that acts only on values within that tolerance of an edge; it does not change the histogram definition (definitions["histogram"] stays "1") or feature schema compatibility. On the stored MLV drawings this changes the bin of 1,109 of 389,974 junction smallest gaps (8 bins) and of no segment orientation or curvature value.

  • detect_junctions(): arms are the directions in which each contour leaves the junction neighbourhood (rule = "exit"), independent of contour direction, numbering and closed-contour start vertex; the absolute gap is Euclidean (gap_metric = "euclidean"), so junctions are rotation-invariant.

  • compute_mat(): pixel-centred, tie-invariant average outward flux (aof = "centered", which requires samples divisible by 4); a skeleton with no removable pixel left (morphology = "minimal": MATLAB-exact hit-or-miss thinning, "hmt8", followed by removal of every remaining simple pixel with at least two neighbours; 2x2 blocks remain only where no pixel is simple); branch tracing, scoring and mapping that do not depend on branch direction, numbering or loop start (branch_rule = "invariant"). Isolated closed loops are scored with circular windows. skeletonize() and trace_contours() use the same thinning.

  • Default branch tracing (branch_rule = "invariant", definition direction-symmetric-tiemax-graph-2) no longer deletes small shapes. min_branch_points now removes only spurs (paths from an end pixel to a junction), shortest first, joining paths through every pixel where nothing else branches; tied spurs are kept together when removing them would leave their junction with fewer than two paths, and no skeleton component loses its last path. A 20 px square previously had no branch and no mapped score; its four arms are now kept and all 80 contour pixels are mapped. The result does not depend on scan order, start pixel or lattice orientation. Specifications and cached MATs with the -graph-1 definition are rejected.

  • Default branch scores are NA where their estimator is undefined, not 0 (branch_rule = "invariant", definition direction-symmetric-tiemax-graph-defined-3; MLV-M033). The published estimator scores the end points of parallelism and taper (zero-width window), branches of fewer than three points, and mirror on three or fewer points as 0, and its width-3 moving mean averages that 0 into the next point. The default marks them NA and averages only defined values, so a branch end takes the value of its defined neighbour (before smoothing); traversal directions, score images and contour mapping combine defined values only. The default also sums each smoothing window directly: the published cumulative-sum differences can round a radius pair (1, 1) below 1 and turn an exact separation of 0 into NA. A raw score of exactly 0 is a defined value and is never replaced by NA. score_branch() and branch_rule = "mlv2023" keep the published values. Compared with the published estimator, scores change at undefined points and the points whose smoothing window contains one, and, for separation, around radius pairs that the published sums round below 1; elsewhere they agree to rounding (at most 3.1e-13 on twelve sampled Forest drawings). On the 2,757 stored drawings per-contour parallelism correlates 0.811 with the published values (0.926 before), whose branch ends are lowered by those zeros; separation and mirror are unchanged (0.982, 0.864). Specifications and cached MATs with the -graph-2 definition are rejected.

  • split_contours() no longer fails when a contour has no finite medial-axis score (more common now that undefined scores are NA): such contours cannot be ranked, so they are left unassigned, scored NA and listed in the new unranked element. Ranks are taken among rankable contours; the length budget is still a fraction of the total length of all contours.

  • Skeleton pixels lying on ink are excluded before branch tracing.

  • mlv_drawing() treats segments whose endpoints differ only by rounding residue as zero-length.

Documentation and plotting

  • New vignettes: getting-started (from a line drawing to contour features), junctions, medial-axis and mlv-compatibility; workflows now covers file input, extraction and feature recipes.
  • New plot.mlv_mat() shows each medial-axis stage (ink, distance, flux, skeleton, branches, scores) in image coordinates with labelled legends.
  • plot.mlv_drawing() draws colour bars with units, uses a cyclic palette for orientation, can draw junction arms, frames the canvas on the raster extent so drawings and MAT stages overlay exactly, and draws mapped scores as filled pixels.
  • detect_junctions() returns an arms list-column with each junction’s arm directions; angles are the gaps between consecutive arms.

Revisions in this port

  • Junction arm angles no longer depend on the merged junction position, and gapped T-junctions no longer gain an additional arm (MLV-R005-R008, R014).
  • Sweep and exhaustive junction search agree exactly, including gaps exactly at the extension limit, independent of segment direction (MLV-R015).
  • Dropping rounding-residue segments keeps contours exactly connected and closed (MLV-R016).
  • Width-1 rasterization is independent of segment direction (MLV-R010).
  • Coincident branch points no longer produce NaN tangents (MLV-R011).

mlvtoolbox 0.2.1

  • Orientation, length and curvature histograms are computed in a fused native pass directly from contours. Measured feature_table() workloads are 3.8-9.4x faster than 0.2.0; all 122 baseline public outputs and their metadata are unchanged (see docs/FUSED_STATISTICS.md).
  • Added contour graph descriptors: source-linked topology, continuation, parallel relations and strict enclosure, with calibrated cache validation and rejection of stale geometry, parameters and calibration.
  • Credited the original MLV, Python AOF and GNU Octave image contributors in Authors@R, added software and methods citations, and installed the full applicable license texts and original notices.

mlvtoolbox 0.2.0

Subsequent candidate: whole-contour stimulus design

  • Added a bounded exact subset designer with set-level matching, optional per-drawing constraints, raw histogram L1 tolerances and explicit resource limits. Optimal, feasible, infeasible and exhausted outcomes are distinct.
  • Results retain original contour identities, input geometry/calibration, reconstructed conditions, independently recomputed constraints and optional fresh junction/MAT diagnostics. A complete stimulus-design vignette is included.

Feature contracts and estimators

  • Prediction now requires the actual training feature schema and rejects bin, predictor, unit, and method mismatches before invoking a model. An explicit warning-emitting legacy bypass remains available.
  • Added versioned feature specifications with fixed bins, pixels-per-degree calibration, physical curvature scales and branch windows, and extraction provenance. Batch statistics and CSV sidecars preserve measurement metadata.
  • Added vertex-turning and arc-length tent curvature estimators, closed-contour wraparound, and exact integration of affine curvature into histograms.
  • Added arc-length branch scores with independent analytical and invariance tests. These are explicitly versioned alternative geometric definitions.
  • Published mlv2023 contour and branch behavior remains the default for one release. Existing numeric parity fixtures remain unchanged.
  • Geometry changes invalidate derived measurements; incompatible MAT caches are rejected. Mapping coverage distinguishes missing scores from valid zero.
